all_videos_in_window.description:
The Elizabeth Islands are one of my favorite places to chase false albacore. Functioning as a natural barrier, they separate Buzzards Bay from Vineyard Sound. The archipelago offers a fascinating mix of complete isolation, ultra-wealthy privacy, and raw New England history.⁠
⁠
When conditions align, baitfish will congregate along the islands drawing the albies in. During this trip with @flatlinercharters from September of a few years ago, the albies were feeding on bay anchovies and readily attacking the Dart 110S from Monomoy Tackle.⁠
⁠

all_videos_in_window.description:
There's been fish cruising in shallow this August. A few subtle twitches, let it slither through the vegetation, and if you're lucky…hooked up!⁠
⁠
The single hook on soft plastics like the Super Snax means you can work right through the weeds without getting hung up. It also makes releasing fish a lot easier.⁠
⁠
Really been loving this style of fishing on my lighter 8'6" rod — makes fighting fish way more fun.⁠
⁠

"Rigging a soft plastic for striper fishing 101". The most important thing in my opinion is to make sure the soft plastic is rigged perfectly straight. Here I'm using a pearl Super Snax from with a size 7/0 twist lock hook, which makes rigging simple and easy.⁠

This bass surely wasn't the biggest of my season, but I was happy to catch it. In a time when big older bass seem to outnumber the younger fish, I am more than happy to be catching schoolies. Especially on a perfectly calm warm morning, while fishing in my bathing suit during sunrise! I will no doubt be dreaming about this day come January.⁠
⁠

all_videos.title: Albie Fishing the Elizabeth Islands off Cape Cod
all_videos.description:
The Elizabeth Islands are one of my favorite places to chase false albacore. Functioning as a natural barrier, they separate Buzzards Bay from Vineyard Sound. The archipelago offers a fascinating mix of complete isolation, ultra-wealthy privacy, and raw New England history.⁠
⁠
When conditions align, baitfish will congregate along the islands drawing the albies in. During this trip with @flatlinercharters from September of a few years ago, the albies were feeding on bay anchovies and readily attacking the Dart 110S from Monomoy Tackle.⁠
⁠
Reeling for a few seconds, and then pausing to allow the lure to sink through the water column, generated bites for me on this trip. But sometimes the albies want the lure skipping along the surface. I have even heard of anglers from MFCC catching them by …

all_videos.title: Fishing Weed Beds Without Getting Hung Up
all_videos.description:
There's been fish cruising in shallow this August. A few subtle twitches, let it slither through the vegetation, and if you're lucky…hooked up!⁠
⁠
The single hook on soft plastics like the Super Snax means you can work right through the weeds without getting hung up. It also makes releasing fish a lot easier.⁠
⁠
Really been loving this style of fishing on my lighter 8'6" rod — makes fighting fish way more fun.⁠
⁠
Tight lines! 🎣⁠

all_videos.title: Striper Fishing with the Super Snax Soft Plastic Lure
all_videos.description:
This August I fished a shallow, weedy spot loaded with striped bass using the pearl Super Snax — a large soft plastic lure that casts noticeably farther than similar baits like Slugos. In this video I'll show you how I like to fish this lure to catch stripers during the middle of bright and sunny summer days on Cape Cod.

The Super Snax's single-hook design also made for quick, easy, pliers-free release — a big plus when you're working through heavy weeds and want fish back in the water fast.

all_videos.title: How to Rig a Soft Plastic for Striper Fishing 101
all_videos.description:
"Rigging a soft plastic for striper fishing 101". The most important thing in my opinion is to make sure the soft plastic is rigged perfectly straight. Here I'm using a pearl Super Snax from with a size 7/0 twist lock hook, which makes rigging simple and easy.⁠
⁠
This bass surely wasn't the biggest of my season, but I was happy to catch it. In a time when big older bass seem to outnumber the younger fish, I am more than happy to be catching schoolies. Especially on a perfectly calm warm morning, while fishing in my bathing suit during sunrise! I will no doubt be dreaming about this day come January.⁠
